name: Choriocarcinoma of the Central Nervous System

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No formal standardized criteria; diagnosis based on histopathology and clinical findings

criteria.description: Histopathological confirmation of choriocarcinoma cells in CNS tissue
Markedly elevated serum beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG) levels
Neuroimaging (MRI/CT) showing intracranial mass with hemorrhagic and necrotic features
Exclusion of extracranial primary choriocarcinoma (e.g., gonadal or gestational origin)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation plus elevated serum β-hCG and characteristic neuroimaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of metastatic choriocarcinoma from other primary sites.

searchTerms: rapid onset of focal nerve problems
fast progression of localized brain deficits

pathognomonic.symptomName: Intracranial hemorrhage presenting with sudden severe headache
searchTerms: sudden severe headache from brain bleed

pathognomonic.symptomName: Markedly elevated serum beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG) levels

common.symptomName: Nausea and vomiting due to increased intracranial pressure
searchTerms: feeling sick from increased brain pressure

common.symptomName: Visual disturbances including diplopia or visual field defects
searchTerms: loss of parts of visual field

common.symptomName: Cognitive impairment or altered mental status

searchTerms: fluid buildup in brain from tumor blockage
brain swelling due to blocked fluid flow
water on the brain caused by tumor

occasional.symptomName: Endocrine dysfunction due to hypothalamic or pituitary involvement
searchTerms: hormone problems from brain gland damage
endocrine imbalance due to brain lesion
cranial nerve palsies causing facial or eye problems

rare.symptomName: Intracranial hypertension syndrome without mass effect
searchTerms: high pressure inside skull without tumor mass
raised brain pressure without visible tumor

laboratory: Markedly elevated serum beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG)
CSF analysis may show elevated β-hCG and malignant cells
Normal or mildly elevated other tumor markers (AFP usually negative)
imaging: MRI showing hemorrhagic, necrotic intracranial mass with surrounding edema
CT scan revealing hyperdense lesion with evidence of bleeding
Possible hydrocephalus due to ventricular obstruction
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; diagnosis based on histopathology
other: Histopathology demonstrating biphasic pattern of cytotrophoblast and syncytiotrophoblast cells
Immunohistochemistry positive for β-hCG and cytokeratin

distinguishingFeatures: Less hemorrhagic tumor appearance on imaging
Presence of primary tumor outside CNS (uterus, gonads)
Different histological pattern with glial origin
Typical imaging features of glioma without hemorrhagic choriocarcinoma pattern

redFlags: Sudden onset severe headache with neurological deterioration
Markedly elevated serum β-hCG without evidence of extracranial primary tumor
references: Nishimura Y, et al. Primary intracranial choriocarcinoma: clinical features and treatment outcomes. J Neurooncol. 2019;142(3):507-515.
